Brimstone
BRIM-stone
noun
From the Middle English brinston, “burning stone” (Old English bryne, a burning, + stan, stone) — sulphur, which takes fire readily and burns with a choking blue flame and a stench.

Biblical Definition

Brimstone is the burning stone — sulphur, which kindles at a touch, burns with a livid flame and a suffocating reek, and leaves the ground it has fallen on barren. Scripture reserves it almost wholly for judgment, and the pattern begins at Sodom: “Then the LORD rained upon Sodom and upon Gomorrah brimstone and fire from the LORD out of heaven” (Gen 19:24). That was no natural disaster overtaking a city; it was rain, sent, by name, from the LORD out of heaven, upon cities whose sin was very grievous. The Psalmist makes it the portion of every wicked man: “Upon the wicked he shall rain snares, fire and brimstone, and an horrible tempest: this shall be the portion of their cup” (Psa 11:6). Christ Himself takes up Sodom’s overthrow and sets it as the very type of the day of His revealing: “But the same day that Lot went out of Sodom it rained fire and brimstone from heaven, and destroyed them all” (Luk 17:29) — even thus shall it be in the day when the Son of man is revealed. And the Revelation carries the word to its final use: the beast, the false prophet, and the devil are cast into the lake of fire and brimstone, where they shall be tormented day and night for ever and ever (Rev 20:10); and “the fearful, and unbelieving… and all liars, shall have their part in the lake which burneth with fire and brimstone: which is the second death” (Rev 21:8). The word is a warning, and it is spoken by Christ oftener than by anyone.

Webster 1828 Definition

Sulphur; the burning stone that kindles at a touch — in Scripture the settled emblem of divine judgment and of the lake of fire.

BRIMSTONE, sulphur; a hard, brittle, inflammable substance which burns with a blue flame and a suffocating odour.

From Middle English brinston — Old English bryne, “a burning,” + stan, “stone.”

The LORD rained brimstone and fire upon Sodom and Gomorrah out of heaven (Gen 19:24).

It is the portion of the cup of the wicked (Psa 11:6).

The lake which burneth with fire and brimstone is the second death (Rev 21:8).

Key Scripture

Gen 19:24 — "Then the LORD rained upon Sodom and upon Gomorrah brimstone and fire from the LORD out of heaven;"

Psa 11:6 — "Upon the wicked he shall rain snares, fire and brimstone, and an horrible tempest: this shall be the portion of their cup."

Luk 17:29 — "But the same day that Lot went out of Sodom it rained fire and brimstone from heaven, and destroyed them all."

Rev 21:8 — "But the fearful, and unbelieving, and the abominable, and murderers, and whoremongers, and sorcerers, and idolaters, and all liars, shall have their part in the lake which burneth with fire and brimstone: which is the second death."

Modern Corruption

The plainest word in Scripture for eternal punishment, denied outright by universalism, extinguished by annihilationism, and mocked into silence by the sneer “fire and brimstone.”

expand to see more

Three corruptions attack this word, and all three end in the same place. Universalism holds that God will at last save every soul, that hell is a purge and not a portion, and that the lake of fire empties. Scripture does not permit it: the same adjective that measures the life of the righteous measures the punishment of the wicked (Mat 25:46), and the Revelation says the tormenting is day and night for ever and ever (Rev 20:10). Annihilationism grants the fire and denies the duration, teaching that the lost are consumed and cease to be. But a fire that never shall be quenched (Mar 9:43) and a smoke of torment that ascendeth up for ever (Rev 14:11) is not a fire that finishes its work in an hour. The third corruption is not an argument at all but a sneer: fire-and-brimstone preaching, used to shame any man who warns his hearers of what Christ warned His. It is worth remembering who preached this doctrine most. The gentlest lips that ever spoke are the lips that said everlasting fire.

There is no way to be kind about hell except to tell the truth about it. The LORD Jesus set Sodom’s burning before His disciples as the pattern of the day of His revealing, and He did it to save them from it. That is what the doctrine is for. Sodom is preached in the New Testament as an example (2Pe 2:6; Jud 7) — a city given over, warned, and consumed — and set alongside it stands Lot, dragged out by the hand while he lingered, saved not by his merit but by the mercy of God. That is every believer’s history. The brimstone fell the same day Lot went out; not before, not after. Judgment waited on the deliverance of the elect, and it always does. So the word is not a bludgeon but an alarm, and the man who hears it and flees to Christ will find that the fire which is the portion of the wicked’s cup was drunk to the dregs by Another in his stead.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

The word means “burning stone” — sulphur, the settled emblem of God’s judgment.

expand to see more

Brimstone — Old English bryne (“a burning”) + stan (“stone”).

It names sulphur: quick to kindle, choking in its smoke, sterile where it falls.

Sodom’s overthrow is the pattern: brimstone and fire from the LORD out of heaven (Gen 19:24).

It is the portion of the cup of the wicked (Psa 11:6) — a measured, judicial draught.

Its last use is the lake of fire and brimstone, the second death (Rev 21:8).

Usage

"The LORD rained brimstone upon Sodom: judgment sent by name, from heaven."

"Fire and brimstone is the portion of their cup — a measured, judicial portion."

"The same day that Lot went out, it rained fire — judgment waits on the rescue of the elect."
